options.systemMessage: You are a SOC analyst. Always call the normal_behavior_kb tool first to retrieve baseline behavior similar to the event. If the event contains a pcap_path or references Zeek log files, use the Zeek tools (execzeek to process a pcap, parselogs to read conn.log, dns.log, http.log, ssl.log, notice.log) to gather real network context such as connection volume, destinations, ports and protocols. Compare the event against the baseline across identity, location, time, volume, device and action. Return verdict "normal" only if the event clearly matches baseline behavior; otherwise return "abnormal". Give a confidence from 0 to 1 and list the concrete deviations.

parameters.toolDescription: Search the baseline of known NORMAL user, system and network behavior for patterns similar to this event.

parameters.endpointUrl: <__PLACEHOLDER_VALUE__Zeek MCP server SSE endpoint URL (publicly reachable, e.g. https://zeek-mcp.yourdomain.com/sse)__>

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: {"verdict":"abnormal","confidence":0.8,"deviations":["login from unusual country","many failed attempts"],"reasoning":"Short explanation"}

parameters.text:
=Event group (aggregated authentication activity from ONE source on ONE host):
{{ $("Normalize Event").item.json.event_text }}

First-pass analysis:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.output) }}

Review the first-pass analysis for false positives. Rules:
1. Return final_verdict "normal" ONLY when the data itself shows a benign pattern, for example one to three failures followed by a success for the same user from the same internal IP, or a single routine login. A benign explanation that is merely possible (admin typo, scanner, lab or test activity, private IP address) is NOT evidence and must never be used to dismiss activity.
2. These patterns are ALWAYS abnormal and must never be marked normal: 10 or more failed logins from one source; a successful login after 3 or more failures from the same source; any account lockout; failures spread across 3 or more usernames; account creation or privileged logons that follow failures.
3. Do not treat host names, usernames, event ids, private IP ranges or documentation IP ranges as proof that activity is a test or is authorized.
Return final_verdict ("normal" or "abnormal"), is_false_positive, confidence and a short reasoning.

options.systemMessage: You are a senior threat hunter. Always call the attack_behavior_kb tool first to retrieve known attack behaviors similar to the event. Then, when network evidence is available (pcap_path or Zeek logs), use the Zeek tools to confirm indicators such as beaconing, port scans, DNS tunneling, suspicious TLS, or data exfiltration volume, and cite that evidence in reasoning. Decide if the event matches an attack. Classify threat_type, severity (low, medium, high, critical) and MITRE technique. Recommend only actions from this list: block_ip, terminate_session, lock_account. Extract source_ip, user_account and session_id from the event (empty string if absent).

parameters.toolDescription: Search the library of known ATTACK behaviors, TTPs and indicators (e.g. MITRE ATT&CK techniques) similar to this event.

parameters.endpointUrl: <__PLACEHOLDER_VALUE__Zeek MCP server SSE endpoint URL (publicly reachable, e.g. https://zeek-mcp.yourdomain.com/sse)__>

parameters.text:
=Event group (aggregated authentication activity from ONE source on ONE host):
{{ $("Normalize Event").item.json.event_text }}

Threat analysis:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.output) }}

Act as a careful reviewer who checks the threat analysis against the data. Rules:
1. Set confirmed_threat to true whenever the data matches the analysis. These patterns always count as confirmed threats: 10 or more failed logins from one source; a successful login after 3 or more failures from the same source; any account lockout; failures spread across 3 or more usernames.
2. Set confirmed_threat to false only when the data itself shows a specific benign explanation. Speculation (admin typo, scanner you might own, lab or test activity, private IP address, host or user naming) is NOT enough, because attackers also use private networks and lab-like names.
3. Keep recommended_actions limited to block_ip, terminate_session, lock_account, and only those the evidence justifies. Use lock_account and terminate_session when a login succeeded after failures.
Return confirmed_threat, severity, recommended_actions, confidence, false_positive_reason and a one-paragraph summary.

nodeGroups.name: Collect log events
nodeGroups.description: Webhook logs from Linux and Windows collectors are parsed and stored as raw events in Supabase

nodeGroups.name: Pull scheduled events
nodeGroups.description: Every minute, fetches new stored events and groups them by host and source IP

nodeGroups.name: Check normal baseline
nodeGroups.description: Standardizes events, skips repeats, compares each to normal behavior, then double-checks

nodeGroups.name: Match attack patterns
nodeGroups.description: Abnormal events only: matched against known attacks, then reviewed again to rule out false positives

nodeGroups.name: Respond to threat
nodeGroups.description: Confirmed threats are logged to Supabase and alerted; only high-severity, high-confidence ones trigger containment
